newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 97/98 growth seen over two pct--Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Japan 97/98 growth seen over two pct--Sakakibara.

text.p: Japan's economic growth is likely to exceed two percent in the current 1997/98 fiscal year after expanding at a rate of nearly three percent in 1996/97, senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara told Reuters in an interview on Friday.
Those forecasts are higher than government's official targets of 2.5 percent growth for 1996/97, which ended on March 31, and 1.9 percent for 1997/98.
"The possibility of the Japanese economy contracting is less than what people think," Sakakibara said in the interview with Reuters Financial Television.

He said an increase in Japan's sales tax to five percent from three percent on April 1 and the scrapping of special income tax cuts in the current fiscal year did not seem to be having a negative impact on overall consumption.
Real estate prices are likely to rebound, he said.
"The peak of the problem of non-performing loans is over. It looks like major Japanese banks can dispose of problem loans within the next two to three years," he said.
"It is irrational to think that the Japanese economy is going to plunge... At the moment, the upside risk for the Japanese economy is bigger than the downside risk," he said.
Sakakibara also said Japan's surplus in trade of goods and services is likely to fall over the medium and long terms.
"The surplus now accounts for 0.5 percent of Japan's GDP (gross domestic product) and the ratio is the smallest among the Group of Seven (G7) countries which enjoy a surplus," he said.
His remarks about the trade surplus came amid fears of rising trade friction with the United States after U.S. officials expressed concern about an increase in the Japanese surplus.
"The surplus in goods and services trade is not likely to increase substantially in 1997/98, although there could be some deviation from the trend in individual months," he said.
